situation:
You are the member relations coordinator at NORTHFIELD VOICE, a call center operator owned by the members who work in it. The general manager (judge), elected by those members, has asked you to recommend how the co-operative should staff its overnight desk while a complaint filed by one member against another is investigated.

NORTHFIELD VOICE handles customer support lines for a handful of clients. Its largest contract, roughly a third of the year's revenue, requires an overnight desk that answers within a set time, and it comes up for renewal in six weeks. One team lead is the only member currently certified to run that desk.

A member on the overnight shift has filed a harassment complaint naming that team lead, over off-hours posts on the team lead's personal social account. The co-operative's policy keeps the details confidential and states no finding until the investigation closes, which will take longer than six weeks. Both members work the same overnight shift in the meantime.

Leaving the team lead on the desk until the renewal is decided protects the revenue that contract brings this year, and it leaves the complainant working the same shift while every member watches how the co-operative handles a complaint. Moving the team lead off the desk puts a member still in training on the overnight lines, and response times slip in the weeks the client is reviewing the renewal.

The general manager (judge) wants your recommendation on the overnight staffing and on what may be said, to whom, while the investigation runs. The general manager (judge) will greet you, hear your ideas and ask questions. When you have finished answering, the general manager (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the general manager of NORTHFIELD VOICE, elected by the members who own the co-operative. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the member relations coordinator to recommend who should run the overnight desk while the complaint is investigated, and to tell you what may be said, and to whom, without going past what the co-operative's policy allows.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of each participant:
judgeQuestions: How would you tell the member this decision affects most what we decided?
What can we say to that member without breaking confidentiality?
